## Outcome

The composer and chips bar match `reference/screens/fullbleed-1440-{dark,light}-thread.png`, `-chips.png` and `-draft.png`, plus the 390 variants:
- **Composer:** a single row with a 38px rounded textarea (placeholder "Message the Khala", accent focus ring, autosizing to 140px) and a 38px round accent send button with the SVG arrow (opacity .35 when disabled, scale .92 when pressed).
- **Chips bar above it:**
  - the first 3 mention chips (the viewer's agents first), then `+N`

  - clicking a chip inserts `@label `

## Scope

1. **`ChatComposer` API (publish first; KM-182 and KM-183 consume it):**
   ```ts
   export type MentionTarget = Readonly<{
     id: string;                       // participantId
     kind: 'human' | 'agent';
     label: string;                    // inserted after '@' (agent label, e.g. "Claude"; human first name)
     display: string;                  // chip text after '@' (agent: label + optional " #suffix"; human: first name)
     hue: number; ownerHue: number;    // from participantHue (KM-180)
     ownerInitials: string;            // agent: owner's; human: own
     harness?: 'claude' | 'codex';
     ownerId: string;
     isViewer: boolean;                // viewer's own human entry
   }>;
   export function ChatComposer(props: Readonly<{
     value: string; onChange(value: string): void; onSend(): void;
     disabled?: boolean; sendDisabled?: boolean; sendDescriptionId?: string;
     placeholder?: string;             // default "Message the Khala"
     mentionTargets?: readonly MentionTarget[];
     chipsOpen?: boolean; onChipsOpenChange?(open: boolean): void;   // controlled, so KM-183 can close the chips when the roster opens
   }>): JSX.Element;
   export function insertMention(value: string, label: string): string;   // khInsert rule: add ' ' if value is non-empty and doesn't end in whitespace, then '@'+label+' '
   ```
   The `participants` prop is **removed**.
2. **Chips** (§9): grouping, order, threshold and DOM exactly as specified. The grid hides the viewer row when the viewer has no agents. The "You" chip is a `span.kh-chip-me`. The toggle chevron path is `m6 15 6-6 6 6` with `stroke-width="2.6"`. The labels are `+{n−3}` / `Less`. When open, the bar has `.kh-to.is-open` and the `khUp` animation.
3. **Composer** (§10): DOM and verbatim CSS.
   - Keep the existing autosize (38→140px, 40px floor at ≤760, width ResizeObserver) from `ConversationLayout.tsx:82-103`.
   - Keep Enter / Shift+Enter and the IME guard from `:109-113`.
   - Replace the `↑` text with the §18 send SVG, at 18px, `stroke-width="2.4"`.
   - `aria-label="Send"`; a visually hidden `<label>` "Message".
4. **CSS** in `ui/khala/composer.css`: §9 CSS + §10 CSS verbatim, with `html[data-theme="light"]` re-rooted, plus the D1 fix line `.khala-app[data-theme="light"] .kh-chip-h { color: hsl(var(--oh) 60% 36%); }`. The unscoped design line 604 must **not** be copied.
5. The chips bar is rendered by `ChatComposer` as a sibling **above** the `<form>`. The composer returns a fragment: `.kh-to` then `form.kh-comp`. `.kh-to + .kh-comp` removes the top border.
6. Delete `.conversation-composer*` and `.conversation-participant*` CSS (`conversation.css:11,41,71-87`).

## Non-goals

- Building `mentionTargets` from the roster and passing them at the `TimelineScreen` call site: **KM-182**.
- Closing the chips when the roster opens, and `@ Mention` in detail: **KM-183** (it calls `onChipsOpenChange(false)` and `insertMention`).
- Parsing and rendering mentions inside messages: **KM-182**.

## Contract and invariants

- **Flat order:** for each group (the viewer first, then humans in member order), the human chip (skipped for the viewer), then that human's agents.
- **Toggle:** only when there are more than 3 chips.
- **Chips are buttons** with `data-kh-mention`, except the "You" chip.
- **Insert result:** `insertMention('hi', 'Claude')` → `'hi @Claude '`; `insertMention('', 'Maya')` → `'@Maya '`; `insertMention('hi ', 'Kai')` → `'hi @Kai '`.
- **Send:** disabled while `!value.trim() || disabled || sendDisabled`.

### Worked example

Targets, with the viewer Kevin (hue 214) owning `Claude`, and Maya (330) owning `Codex`:

```html
<div class="kh-to">
  <div class="kh-to-flat" role="toolbar" aria-label="Mention">
    <button type="button" class="kh-chip kh-chip-a" style="--oh:214" data-kh-mention="a1"><img src="…claude-symbol.svg" alt="">@Claude<i>KE</i></button>
    <button type="button" class="kh-chip kh-chip-h" style="--oh:330" data-kh-mention="p-maya"><i>MC</i>@Maya</button>
    <button type="button" class="kh-chip kh-chip-a" style="--oh:330" data-kh-mention="a2"><img src="…codex-color.svg" alt="">@Codex<i>MC</i></button>
  </div>
</div>
<form class="kh-comp"><label class="sr-only" for="kh-input">Message</label><textarea class="kh-input" id="kh-input" rows="1" placeholder="Message the Khala"></textarea><button class="kh-send" type="submit" disabled aria-label="Send"><svg …><path d="M12 19V5M5 12l7-7 7 7"/></svg></button></form>
```

Exactly 3 chips, so there is no toggle. A fourth target adds `<button class="kh-to-tog" aria-expanded="false">+1<svg …/></button>`.

## Test scenarios

- `ui/khala/MentionChips.test.tsx`:
  1. The worked example's order.
  2. 4+ targets → 3 chips + `+N`.
  3. Open → the grid with a `.kh-to-h` for each human, and the viewer row only when the viewer has agents; the footer text is `Mention a human or agent`; the toggle reads `Less` with `aria-expanded="true"`.
  4. Clicking a chip calls `onChange(insertMention(value, label))`.
  5. The "You" chip is a `span`, not a button.
- `ui/conversation/ChatComposer.test.tsx`:
  1. Empty → send disabled.
  2. Typing enables it.
  3. Enter sends; Shift+Enter does not.
  4. IME composition (keyCode 229) does not send.
  5. The placeholder is `Message the Khala`.
  6. The send button contains an `svg`, not the text `↑`.
- `ui/khala/composer.browser` check (inside `features/timeline/timeline.browser.spec.ts` or a new `ui/khala/composer.browser.spec.ts`):
  1. In dark theme, the human chip's computed colour equals `hsl(330 70% 72%)` (D1).
  2. In light theme, it equals `hsl(330 60% 36%)`.
  3. The textarea grows to 140px and then scrolls.
  4. At 390px the chip row scrolls horizontally with no page scroll.
